title: Fights on 52nd Street: soldiers and the night the whole street brawled
summary: Soldiers sent from the South put everyone in a fighting mood; one night Byas, Benny Harris and Teddy Reig were in a street brawl.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So I got back on the job. I say hah, Ben, I say you do that shit to Charlie, I say you'll do it to me too. I say and if you do, man, I'll take a killing, but I ain't going to take no whipping. I say as large as you are, you know. There's no way. He mumbled something, you know. Gazed off into space, like he hasn't even heard me, you know. Well, I was ready for him. Never carried a knife, but I pulled my own coat. I say I'm getting so wild with this fighting, I . I won more fights on 52nd street than Sugar Ray did in the ring. Because I'm fighting civilians plus soldiers. See they sent all of the Southern soldiers north, you know, to brainwash them so to see Negro boys walking down the street with white women, you know. Naturally this put them in a fighting mood right away.

And they sent the northern soldiers south telling them broke their morale not to speak to the Negros you know and this This put everybody in a fighting mood. So one night, it's like D-Day. Kelley's Stables was on 52nd street between Seventh and Eighth and across the street was the Hickory House. Joseph Marsala

Mary McPartland, and Mary Osborne, they were over there a lot you know. It was -- Red Nova worked over there and the next block with -- which was Sixth Avenue and they renamed it that The Avenue of the Stars, between Sixth and Fifth, but the clubs was mostly about midway to the block and then they ended and then the 21 Club was further up the street. And that entailed the Three Deuces, The Downbeat next door, Tony's was like a supper club, they had a gate under the staircase, I forget this woman's name, Bill Holiday loved to hear her sing. She'd go in there when she wanted to get away from the everyday thing you know and hear her sing. She would make the tables, you know sit around the tables and there was the Onyx club that Bill worked in, Jimmy Ryan's next door, the Dixieland Joint. The Yacht Club, The Famous Door.

And all of a sudden in -- it was like D-Day. Everyone emerged into the streets fighting. At the same time. Out of all of the clubs. Don Byas his -- hit somebody in the mouth with his horn; Benny Harris had broke his trumpet across somebody's head. And Teddy Reig, you remember Teddy Reig, big and fat as he has been-- somebody had him down beating the hell out of him, (laughter) a little bitty dude.
Don't tell me it was Pee Wee Marquette.
No, but Dizzy Buff saved him. Dizzy broke a Coca Cola bottle across his, whoever's head that was on Teddy. But everybody was fighting. So one night. --
